clue.text: Point to love perhaps as a subject for this

definitions.text: Point to love perhaps as a subject for this

parts.note: N is north, a point of the compass

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word love may appear in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A suggestion that romance is a fitting theme for some piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' shuffles the four letters after N; read whole, the clue says love is a favourite subject for this kind of book.
explanation.definitionFit: A long work of fiction very often takes romance as its subject.

clue.text: Brewed tea with banana for an old Arab

indicators.note: brewed suggests tea and banana being stirred together into a new mix

explanation.surface: A drink made from tea and banana served to an ancient desert dweller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewed' rearranges TEA and BANANA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nabataeans were an ancient Arab people whose capital was Petra.

clue.text: One of Brooke's hundred predawn dancers

definitions.text: One of Brooke's hundred predawn dancers

parts.words: One of Brooke's hundred predawn dancers
parts.note: refers to Rupert Brooke's poem Grantchester, in which a hundred clergymen dance on the lawn before dawn

explanation.surface: A member of a troupe of a hundred dancers in a Brooke poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Grantchester Brooke imagines 'A hundred Vicars down the lawn' dancing before dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's dancing figures are parish priests of the Church of England.

clue.text: Oil for blue car — it's badly needed

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of blue car and it are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the clue's it's is read as it is: IT, with is as a link

explanation.surface: Oil is urgently required for a blue car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges BLUE CAR with IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lubricate a machine is to apply grease to reduce friction.

clue.text: Plant, bird and fish

parts.note: a chick is a young bird
ling is a food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A list of three natural-history items: a plant, a bird and a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface lists three things, but the first is the definition and the other two build it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickling, or chickling vetch, is a leguminous plant grown for fodder.

clue.text: Get in touch with consular head on diplomacy

indicators.note: head points to the opening letter of the word consular

parts.note: tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Approach the head of a consulate about a diplomatic matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To contact someone is to communicate with them.

clue.text: No man can be so cruel — and no error

definitions.text: No man can be so cruel

explanation.surface: Cruelty beyond any human being, and perfection beyond us too.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading leans on 'To err is human': anything free of error is not human at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhuman means brutal beyond human feeling, and, read as in-human, describes what lies outside mortal fallibility.

clue.text: The excitement of football?

parts.note: the thrill of the game and the strikes of the ball share one word

explanation.surface: Wondering what thrills a sport provides.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrills are what people get from things they enjoy, and a footballer's strikes of the ball share the word.

clue.text: Give the copy a slant (including the last letter)

definitions.text: Give the copy a slant (including the last letter)

parts.words: Give the copy a slant (including the last letter)
parts.note: printing text in sloping type, and the spelling here uses Z, the alphabet's final letter

explanation.surface: An editor's instruction to slope the text.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting type in sloping letters, spelt with a Z.

clue.text: 5. but not silly, these old Roman alarmists

definitions.text: 5. but not silly, these old Roman alarmists

parts.words: 5. but not silly, these old Roman alarmists
parts.note: refers to the sacred birds on the Capitol whose cackling warned Rome of a Gallic night attack, and to the phrase silly as a goose

explanation.surface: Ancient Romans who raised the alarm, cruel perhaps but no fools.
explanation.walkthrough: In 390 BC the sacred birds of Juno on the Capitol woke the defenders when the Gauls attacked by night.
explanation.definitionFit: The Capitoline birds that saved Rome by cackling were sacred to Juno.

clue.text: Support magistrates getting seat in Parliament

parts.note: to back is to support
the bench is magistrates collectively

explanation.surface: Someone backing the justices of the peace gets elected to the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbenchers, the ordinary members without office, sit on the rear rows of the Commons.

clue.text: College girl in Ireland

explanation.surface: A young woman at a university college over in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a Cambridge college, a girl's name, and a county in the west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Clare College is at Cambridge, it is a woman's first name, and County Clare lies on Ireland's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: It could make one tear one's hat

indicators.note: could make says the letters of tear and one may be rebuilt into something new

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Something frustrating enough to make a person rip their own headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges TEAR with I (one) into the hat's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A terai is a wide-brimmed felt sun hat, named after a lowland region of India and Nepal.

clue.text: Possibly it's a crime truce

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of it's a crime can form another word

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a ceasefire could count as an offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges the nine letters of IT'S A CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a formal agreement to stop fighting, a ceasefire.

clue.text: Take out additional performance, suffering a loss

indicators.note: suffering a loss means the joined words lose a letter A, the 'a' of the clue

parts.note: extra means additional
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: Removing an encore that went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: EXTRA + ACT gives EXTRAACT; 'suffering a loss' removes one A.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to remove or pull it out.

clue.text: Madness in Stan maybe — due to this devil?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
maybe suggests the letters of Stan may be rearranged

parts.note: mania is madness

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a man called Stan went mad because of some demon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' gives TASN, which 'in' wraps round the madness; the devil is the marsupial named after the island state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian devil is a carnivorous marsupial found in Tasmania.

clue.text: "Gives to airy ---- A local habitation" (M N Dream)

definitions.text: Gives to airy ---- A local habitation" (M N Dream)

parts.words: Gives to airy ---- A local habitation" (M N Dream)
parts.note: a fill-in quotation: the missing word completes Theseus's line about the poet's pen in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A line from Shakespeare with one word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line is 'And gives to airy nothing / A local habitation and a name' (Act 5, Scene 1).
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation's missing word is the airy emptiness that the poet's pen gives shape and a name.

clue.text: Irritability of examiners?

parts.note: read as the quality of those who set exams, a playful coinage from tester

explanation.surface: Asking whether examiners are bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being touchy or tetchy; whimsically, the state of being an examiner.

clue.text: Banger for tea?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sausage could stand in for a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Banger is British for a sausage and also for a firework; the firework sense is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The explosive mixture in fireworks shares its name with a Chinese green tea rolled into pellets.

clue.text: Beginning life in the Northern rising

parts.note: an ascent is a rising

explanation.surface: Something first stirring during a rebellion in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like a revolt, but it is simply an ascent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into existence, emerging.

clue.text: Means to execute policy to nail parasites, say

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: tack is a small nail and ticks are parasites

explanation.surface: A plan to deal with bloodsuckers by pinning them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say': TACK TICKS spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactics are the methods used to carry out a strategy.

clue.text: By implication sailing west from these parts

definitions.text: By implication sailing west from these parts

parts.words: By implication sailing west from these parts
parts.note: a ship heading west must be setting out from the opposite quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A ship heading west from its home waters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lands toward sunrise are the ones a westward voyage would start from.

clue.text: Entangled with decoration in the finish

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: the end is the finish
lace is a decorative trimming

explanation.surface: Caught up in ornamentation at the very end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decoration' looks like a medal, but it is a delicate openwork trimming; 'in' places it within the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlaced means wound about or intertwined.

clue.text: Sort of joke to expect from musical cats

explanation.surface: What sort of prank you would get from singing felines.
explanation.walkthrough: A prank played on someone is one kind of joke; T. S. Eliot's Old Possum's Book of the title cats inspired the stage musical Cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank is a hands-on joke, and Eliot's book that inspired Cats describes its felines with that same adjective.

clue.text: Fear of a god

parts.note: the Greeks credited sudden groundless terror to the goat-footed rural deity

explanation.surface: Dread of a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden terror, named after the Greek god Pan, believed to cause it.

clue.text: Subject of my autobiography

parts.note: the subject of a life story about oneself is, playfully, oneself as topic: the article plus the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: What a memoir is about.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as THE ME, it is what an autobiography is about.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject of a work; split, it names the self that a memoir covers.

clue.text: One millennium since it was an insect? It still is

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
M stands for a thousand, the Roman numeral
ago as in long since, back in time

explanation.surface: A creature that was a bug a thousand years ago and is still one now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It still is' plays on the adult stage: an insect that has reached its final form stays that way.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the final, fully adult stage of an insect.

clue.text: Man, for instance, follows a way of the Church

indicators.note: follows means the island comes after the a

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an island

explanation.surface: A man joins in a religious way of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between the pews in a church.

clue.text: What a row when I put in the leading feature!

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the nose is the face's most prominent, leading feature

explanation.surface: An exclamation of alarm at a row once someone takes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places I inside NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is loud sound, a din or racket.

clue.text: Can't be stumped with the number grown

parts.note: in cricket a batsman with bat grounded inside the batting line, in his crease, cannot be stumped
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A cricketer safe from stumping while the score has risen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the line the batsman stands behind; once his bat is grounded inside it he cannot be stumped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something increased has become larger, enlarged.

clue.text: Look over studies by journalist as summarized

parts.note: to con is to study or look over
dens are studies, private rooms for work
ED is an editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone reviewing research papers alongside a reporter who has written a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed means made shorter, abridged.

clue.text: Mere cut, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to shear is to cut

explanation.surface: A remark that a slice is nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer can mean nothing but, utter, as in sheer luck.
